 (Sunil Jatav Vs The State Of Madhya Prad
 Dated : 11-11-2024
 Mr. Ravi Dwivedi - Advocate for the appellant.
 Mr. Yogesh Parashar - Public Prosecutor for respondent/
Heard on I.A.No. 12139 of 2024, first application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. for suspension of
sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
The appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 374 of the Cr.P.C.
against the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 01.06.2024 passed by Additional
Special Judge (Pocso Act) and Xiii Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior District Gwalior (M.P.) in
Sc No.43/2023

sentences.text:
whereby, appellant has been convicted and sentenced under Section 376(2)(N) of
Ipc to undergo rigorous imprisonment of ten years with fine of Rs.500/- and under Section 506
Part-II of Ipc to undergo rigorous imprisonment of five years with fine of Rs.500/-with default
stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Court below has wrongly convicted the appellant without appreciating the materials available on record.
It is further argued that the learned trial Court at para 18 of the judgment hold that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was not minor and was a major woman.
Further submission is that statement of prosecutrix clearly indicates that this is a case of consent.
During cross examination, prosecutrix has admitted that the incident occurred six months back from date of filing of FIR.

As per her allegation, appellant had some obscene photographs and therefore, she did not refuse for physical relationship, however, prosecution has failed to seize mobile, camera or any photographs of the prosecutrix.
Further submission is that the statement of prosecutrix further reveals that earlier also she has lodged report against various person about her sexual assault.
Since 2 CRA-7040-2024 prosecutrix is a major and this is the case of consent, therefore, DNA report looses its significance.
Under all these circumstances so also in light of the fact that appellant has already served 9 months of incarceration out of total jail sentence awarded to him.
The appeal is likely to take long time to come up for final hearing and the appellant has h o p e and believe that he would succeed.

Hence, he prayed to suspend the jail sentence and Sunil Jatav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25520294/
1 grant of bail to appellant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned State counsel opposed the application and prayed for rejection of the same.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on merits of the case, application (I.A. No. 12139 of 2024) is allowed and it is directed that subject to depositing of fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant shall remain suspended and he be released on bail.
He is further directed to mark his presence before the Registry of this Court on 18.12.2024 and on subsequent dates as may be given in this regard.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
A copy of this order be sent to the concerned Court below for compliance.
